title: Microplastics and Heavy Metals in Prepared Meals: What to Know
summary: Discover how microplastics and heavy metals enter prepared meals, what clinical research reveals, and how third-party lab testing ensures food safety.
body_text: In short How heavy metals and microplastics enter the food chain For anyone managing their health with clinical precision, a fundamental question arises: how do toxins find their way into clean, whole ingredients? The answer lies in the soil and water that feed our agricultural systems. Industrial runoff, municipal waste, and agricultural chemical runoff deposit toxic heavy metals like lead, arsenic, and cadmium into farm soils and irrigation channels. Meanwhile, the fragmentation of agricultural plastics, such as plastic mulching and greenhouse films, sheds millions of microscopic plastic particles directly into the soil. Root absorption in crops: Plants draw up heavy metals from soil, mistaking them for essential nutrients like zinc and iron. Aquatic bioaccumulation: Microplastics and heavy metals wash into oceans, where they are ingested by marine life and climb up the food chain. Trophic transfer: Livestock and poultry ingest contaminated feed, concentrating these persistent toxins in their tissues before reaching consumer plates. This environmental accumulation is not a hypothetical risk; it is a documented reality. Research on microplastics confirms that these sub-5mm particles are now fully integrated into the terrestrial food web, entering the roots of wheat and vegetables and traveling into the human digestive tract. Once in the body, heavy metals and plastic particles can disrupt metabolic pathways, damage organ systems, and impact long-term cellular health. This makes standard organic certifications insufficient on their own, as soil history and plastic packaging can still introduce unwanted contaminants. At Locale, we address this environmental vulnerability with a strict verification model. We do not simply trust that ingredients are safe; we require proof. Through our Certified Clean High Protein Meal Subscription , every ingredient batch is independently tested by Light Labs for heavy metals, pesticides, PFAS, and microplastic-related toxins like phthalates . To prevent post-cooking contamination, we deliver our high-protein prepared meals in reusable, plastic-free glass jars . This ensures that our meals remain as clean on your plate as they were in our kitchen. The physical health risks established by clinical research When evaluating prepared food options, understanding the biological impact of environmental toxins is critical for long-term health. Rather than relying on vague wellness warnings, clinical research highlights the concrete mechanisms through which common pesticides and plastics damage human cells. At Locale, we examine this science to guide our strict sourcing standards across the SF Bay Area and Los Angeles, partnering directly with premium local purveyors-including Diestel Family Ranch, Straus Family Creamery, Masa, Lakeside Organic Farms, and Monterey Fish Market-to ensure total ingredient transparency. A study summarized by UCLA Health established a link between agricultural pesticide exposure and neurological decline. Analyzing California farm communities, researchers found that long-term exposure to pesticides is associated with higher rates of Parkinson's disease. This documented risk underscores why avoiding pesticide residues in food is a clinical necessity for long-term health. Similarly, microplastic contamination presents severe risks to reproductive health. A multi-site clinical study investigated the impact of mixed microplastic exposure on male fertility. The study found multiple microplastics in all participants and identified polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), a plastic commonly shed from non-stick cookware and processed packaging, as a key driver linked to lower sperm count and motility. This research confirms that daily microplastics exposure leads to systemic biological accumulation. To eliminate this risk, our Certified Clean High Protein Meal Subscription utilizes reusable glass packaging to keep your food completely clean. Pesticide residue audits to prevent exposure to toxic agricultural chemicals like chlorpyrifos. Microplastic and phthalate screening to verify that food and ingredients remain uncontaminated. Heavy metal analysis to ensure safety from cumulative toxins in the food chain. How independent lab testing intercepts hidden toxins For individuals managing specific health conditions or seeking to minimize environmental toxins, relying on standard food distribution channels is a medical risk. Mass-market prepared foods rarely undergo rigorous vetting for invisible chemical contaminants before they enter your kitchen. To eliminate this blind spot, Locale partners with Light Labs, an independent third-party laboratory, to screen incoming raw ingredients . By conducting objective chemical assays on produce and proteins before any culinary preparation begins, independent screening intercepts hidden contaminants at the source. Heavy Metals: Screening targets bioaccumulative toxins like lead, mercury, arsenic, and cadmium that can build up in human tissues over years . Pesticides: Tests detect synthetic pesticide residues, which is critical given that long-term exposure to agricultural pesticides has been linked to a significantly higher risk of neurodegenerative diseases like Parkinson's disease in regional cohort studies summarized by UCLA Health . Phthalates and PFAS: Chemical screening identifies synthetic endocrine disruptors and 'forever chemicals' that bypass standard municipal food safety audits . Microplastics: Screening filters out microscopic polymer fragments, which recent multi-site research published on ResearchGate has linked directly to cellular dysfunction and reproductive health risks, including impaired sperm motility . Preventing ingestion is vital for preserving metabolic and reproductive integrity. Instead of hiding behind generic claims like 'natural' or 'clean,' we believe health-conscious consumers deserve verifiable validation. This independent screening process ensures that every meal delivered through our Certified Clean High Protein Meal Subscription meets strict physiological safety standards. It also allows us to safely maximize nutrient density with functional inclusions like bone broth-infused rice, edamame noodles, and Greek yogurt-based sauces, delivering the culinary credibility of top local restaurants right to your home. By publishing these independent lab reports, we provide full transparency so you can make informed decisions about your daily nutritional intake without worrying about hidden toxic exposure. Why reusable glass packaging is essential for meal safety Traditional prepared meals are almost always packaged in single-use plastic trays. Even when these containers are labeled microwave-safe, heating them triggers a dramatic release of synthetic polymers. A landmark 2023 study by researchers at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln demonstrated that microwaving plastic food containers can release up to 4.22 million microplastics and 2.11 billion nanoplastics from a single square centimeter of plastic in just three minutes. When these containers are heated, the physical structure of the plastic degrades, shedding microscopic particles directly into the food you eat. This degradation is further accelerated by the high temperatures, fats, and acidic ingredients typical of prepared dishes. For individuals with strict medical or health motivations, this chemical migration is a serious concern. Plastic packaging frequently contains endocrine-disrupting chemicals, such as phthalates and bisphenols, which leach into food and can alter hormonal pathways, impair metabolic function, and increase systemic inflammation. Zero chemical leaching: Unlike plastic, glass does not contain endocrine disruptors like phthalates or bisphenols, meaning no harmful chemicals transfer to your food during storage or heating. No microplastic shedding: Glass is highly durable and structurally stable, ensuring that no microscopic synthetic particles are released into your meals. Safe high-heat reheating: Glass withstands microwave and oven temperatures without degrading, maintaining the absolute purity of your high-protein ingredients. At Locale, we eliminate this exposure risk at the source. Our Certified Clean High Protein Meal Subscription delivers every meal in heavy-duty, reusable glass jars instead of plastic packaging . Glass is completely inert, meaning it will never leach chemicals, phthalates, or microscopic particles into your food, no matter how hot it gets. By opting for sanitized, reusable glass, we provide a genuinely safe, plastic-free reheating experience that preserves the nutritional integrity of your food while actively reducing your cumulative microplastics exposure over time. Frequently asked questions How do microplastics enter prepared meals? Microplastics enter prepared meals through two main pathways: bioaccumulation in the agricultural food supply (where crops and animals absorb microparticles from soil and water) and packaging. When food is cooked, stored, or heated in plastic trays, the polymer bonds degrade, causing plastic particles to leach directly into the food. What heavy metals are most commonly found in prepared foods? The most common heavy metal contaminants are lead, mercury, arsenic, and cadmium. These elements occur naturally but accumulate in the environment due to industrial pollution and chemical fertilizers. Crops absorb them from the soil, allowing them to enter the prepared food supply unless carefully vetted. What does clinical research say about pesticide exposure? Peer-reviewed research has linked chronic pesticide exposure to severe neurological conditions. For example, a retrospective observational study summarized by UCLA Health analyzed California agricultural communities and found that long-term pesticide exposure was associated with higher rates of Parkinson's disease among its 800 participants. How does microplastic exposure affect reproductive health? Clinical studies indicate that microplastics can accumulate in reproductive organs and disrupt function. A multi-site cross-sectional study published on ResearchGate analyzed samples from 113 men and found microplastics in all participants, with higher exposure (particularly to PTFE) linked to lower sperm count and motility. How does Light Labs test Locale's meals for contaminants? Locale partners with Light Labs, an independent third-party analytical laboratory, to screen ingredients before preparation. Light Labs tests for heavy metals (lead, mercury, arsenic, and cadmium), synthetic pesticide residues, phthalates, and PFAS, publishing verified results online to ensure total transparency. Why is glass packaging safer than plastic for prepared meals? Glass is an inert material that does not react with food or degrade when heated. Traditional plastic meal trays, even those labeled BPA-free, can leach endocrine-disrupting chemicals like phthalates and shed microplastics when microwaved. Glass packaging completely eliminates these chemical leaching and contamination risks. Sources uclahealth.org news.unl.edu uclahealth.org

title: Astronics Unveils Mission‑Ready Edge AI for Rugged Avionics Platforms
summary: New Ballard NG3 AI Accelerator offers MOSA-aligned AI edge inference EAST AURORA, NY, July 21, 2026 – Astronics Corporation (Nasdaq: ATRO), a…
body_text: Astronics Unveils Mission‑Ready Edge AI for Rugged Avionics Platforms Download as PDF July 21, 2026 New Ballard NG3 AI Accelerator offers MOSA-aligned AI edge inference EAST AURORA, NY , July 21, 2026 – Astronics Corporation (Nasdaq: ATRO), a leading supplier of advanced technologies and products to the global aerospace, defense, and other mission critical industries, today announced the Ballard NG3 AI Accelerator, a rugged, low‑SWaP edge computing solution designed to bring deployable artificial intelligence to aerospace and defense platforms. The NG3 AI Accelerator combines the Hailo‑8R artificial intelligence (AI) processor with the proven NG3 avionics computing platform to deliver compact, efficient, and rugged edge AI capabilities aligned with Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) principles and commercial off‑the‑shelf (COTS) deployment requirements. NG3 AI Accelerator from Astronics provides a MOSA‑aligned, COTS‑ready aerospace‑grade AI platform that helps defense and aerospace programs rapidly field AI‑enabled capabilities. Delivering up to 13 trillion operations per second (TOPS) of AI inference at approximately 3 TOPS per watt in a small, low‑SWaP form factor, the NG3 AI Accelerator is optimized for airborne edge computing environments where power, space, and environmental margins are tight. Rigorous qualification to DO‑160, MIL‑STD‑810, MIL‑STD‑461, and MIL‑STD‑704 demonstrates its ability to handle shock, vibration, EMI, and power variations typical of helicopters, fixed‑wing aircraft, ground vehicles, and unmanned systems. “Our customers need edge AI solutions they can deploy quickly and confidently,” said Jon Neal, President of Astronics Advanced Electronic Systems. “The Ballard NG3 AI Accelerator delivers a compact, rugged AI platform that seamlessly integrates directly into existing avionics architectures, eliminating additional gateways while enabling efficient, low‑risk deployment of AI capabilities at the edge. It builds on decades of Ballard experience in avionics computing with Hailo’s advanced AI processing to give defense and aerospace programs a COTS‑ready path to fielding AI‑enabled capabilities in a form factor they know they can depend on.” Purpose-built for airborne edge computing, the NG3 AI Accelerator integrates AI processing with native avionics I/O—such as MIL‑STD‑1553, ARINC 429/708/717, discrete I/O, and Ethernet—in a single unit. This allows direct connection to aircraft databuses and sensors without additional protocol converters, reducing system complexity, wiring, and latency while helping minimize overall SWaP. Programs can leverage the NG Family’s existing ecosystem of avionics interfaces and computing platforms to modernize mission architectures without disruptive redesign. At its core, the Hailo‑8R Neural Processing Unit (NPU) delivers efficient, on‑device inference for vision, signal, and sensor‑fusion workloads, supporting a wide range of AI models and frameworks. This broad support enables developers to reuse existing workflows and libraries while tailoring solutions for missions ranging from object detection and tracking to audio processing and on‑board decision support—all within the same compact edge platform. As a flagship member of the Ballard NG Family, the NG3 AI Accelerator provides aerospace and defense programs with a practical path to deploying advanced edge‑AI capabilities on a robust, aerospace‑grade platform. It allows customers to unlock new levels of situational awareness, automation, and responsiveness, without sacrificing SWaP, reliability, or low integration risk. Backed by Astronics’ Ballard brand, a trusted supplier of rugged COTS avionics computing and databus solutions supporting leading defense primes, system integrators, and government agencies worldwide, the NG3 AI Accelerator extends a legacy of proven avionics interface solutions into the era of edge AI For more information, please visit: astronics.com/ng3-ai-accelerator . ABOUT ASTRONICS CORPORATION Astronics Corporation (Nasdaq: ATRO) serves the world’s aerospace, defense, and other mission-critical industries with proven innovative technology solutions. Astronics works side-by-side with customers, integrating its array of power, connectivity, lighting, structures, interiors, and test technologies to solve complex challenges. For over 50 years, Astronics has delivered creative, customer-focused solutions with exceptional responsiveness. Today, global airframe manufacturers, airlines, military branches, completion centers, and Fortune 500 companies rely on the collaborative spirit and innovation of Astronics. The Company’s strategy is to increase its value by developing technologies and capabilities that provide innovative solutions to its targeted markets. Additional information on Astronics and its solutions can be found at Astronics.com. For more information, contact: Astronics AES: Investor Relations: Jeff Solberg, Product Marketing Deborah K. title: Advancing Europe’s Automotive Innovation Ecosystem: Arteris Continues Its Work in the RIGOLETTO Project
summary: As software-defined vehicles reshape the automotive industry, collaborative innovation is becoming essential to developing secure, scalable computing platforms. Learn how Arteris is contributing to the European RIGOLETTO project, helping advance next-generation automotive architectures through expertise in Network-on-Chip technology, RISC-V integration, and high-performance semiconductor design.
body_text: Home » Newsroom » Blog » Advancing Europe’s Automotive Innovation Ecosystem: Arteris Continues Its Work in the RIGOLETTO Project Advancing Europe’s Automotive Innovation Ecosystem: Arteris Continues Its Work in the RIGOLETTO Project Jul 30, 2026 Arteris 2 min read As the automotive industry moves toward software-defined vehicles, the need for open, scalable, and secure computing platforms has never been greater. Developing these platforms requires collaboration across the semiconductor ecosystem, bringing together expertise in processor architectures, AI acceleration, interconnects, memory systems, software tools, and system integration. That collaborative approach is at the heart of RIGOLETTO, one of several European research and innovation projects in which Arteris is proud to participate. On July 7-8, Arteris was represented by Emmanuel Vaumorin at the RIGOLETTO General Assembly in Herzogenaurach, Germany, where consortium members celebrated the successful completion of the project’s first year and aligned on the next phase of development. Supported by the Chips Joint Undertaking, RIGOLETTO brings together 64 leading European semiconductor companies and research organizations from 15 European and associated countries to develop a next-generation automotive hardware platform based on the RISC-V instruction set architecture. The project spans the technologies required to build future software-defined vehicles, including processor cores, AI accelerators, interconnects, memory hierarchies, peripheral subsystems, and software development tools. For Arteris, participation in RIGOLETTO reflects a broader commitment to advancing semiconductor innovation through collaborative research. Across multiple European initiatives, Arteris contributes expertise in high-performance, safety-compliant Network-on-Chip (NoC) IP technology, heterogeneous IP interconnects, RISC-V integration, secure on-chip communication, hardware and software information integration automation including at the hardware-software interface, and the definition and prototyping of next-generation automotive computing platforms. As vehicle architectures become increasingly centralized and software-driven, efficient communication between compute elements is becoming just as important as the compute itself. High-performance interconnect technologies play a critical role in enabling the scalability, safety, and determinism required for next-generation automotive systems, whether those are chiplets, SoCs, or high-end MCUs. Projects like RIGOLETTO demonstrate what can be achieved when industry leaders and research organizations work together toward a common vision. By contributing our expertise in Network-on-Chip technology and advanced chip and chiplet architectures, we are helping build the open, scalable computing platforms that will support the next generation of software-defined vehicles. Emmanuel Vaumorin Director of Strategic Research & Development Programs at Arteris The General Assembly highlighted the strong progress made during the project’s first year and the continued momentum behind Europe’s vision for open automotive computing. As RIGOLETTO moves from architecture definition toward silicon implementation, the consortium is helping establish a secure, certifiable, and scalable foundation for future mobility. RIGOLETTO is one of several collaborative research initiatives supported by Arteris across Europe, reflecting the company’s long-standing commitment to advancing semiconductor technologies through partnership, innovation, and open industry collaboration. The RIGOLETTO project is supported by the Chips Joint Undertaking. Learn more at www.rigoletto-project.eu. title: Get 6 Times Longer Conveyor Belt Life With the KleanTop® PacTitan Pro™ Metal Belt From Regal Rexnord
body_text: Get 6 Times Longer Conveyor Belt Life With the KleanTop® PacTitan Pro™ Metal Belt From Regal Rexnord New 5/8” pitch design option delivers cleaner production and extended belt life. MILWAUKEE, WIS. — Dec. 3, 2024 – Customers in a wide range of food processing industries have extended their conveyor belt service life and reduced downtime with the KleanTop PacTitan Pro Metal Belt from the Regal Rexnord Corporation (NYSE: RRX), a global leader in engineering and manufacturing solutions that power, transmit, and control motion. The PacTitan Pro — now available in a larger pitch size — is an advanced conveying solution for the toughest food processing applications, including battering, breading, glazing, drying, and frying. The cutting-edge, patented conveyor belt design is built to meet many of the demanding requirements found in food processing industries, including small product handling, tight transfers, and harsh applications. The PacTitan Pro has a proven extended service life that is up to six times longer than the average metal conveyorbelt on the market — lowering the risk of unplanned downtime caused by belt failure and improving food and employee safety. Along with improved belt life, users have experienced reduced maintenance time and costs, improved production line uptime, and minimized product contamination. In addition, a new 5/8” belt pitch option with an increased open area provides shorter intervals of excess batter and breading build-up, ensuring a cleaner, more efficient production process. The 75% open area (compared to 65% in the traditional design) allows for superior airflow, making it ideal for baking and snack foodapplications where efficient heat transfer is critical. It’s also 22% lighter than the standard 7/16-inch belt, helping to minimize wear and tear on motors, drive components, and support rails to extend equipment lifespan. “With the PacTitan Pro, teams spend less time on maintenance and repair, buy fewer replacement belts, and get more production hours out of the day,” said Natalie Gray, U.S. Strategic Account Manager for Food & Beverage, Regal Rexnord. “Often, we see end users running this belt for months compared to the weeks that they would run typical wire belts.” In one user example, the PacTitan Pro was tested at a major poultry further processing facility. Their breading, battering, frying, and glazing equipment used a competitor’s standard metal belt that had repetitive weekly and bi-weekly failures, causing ongoing shutdowns and high maintenance costs. The PacTitan Pro was installed and tested for six months without failures under high tension and harsh settings. It lasted 12 times longer than the previous metal belt solution. The groundbreaking belt design delivers key benefits to users, including: Longer belt life , thanks to dedicated sprocket lanes that reduce the amount of bending and distortion within the belt as it engages the sprocket, as well as a fully uniform design on both sides, allowing the belt to be flipped to easily address wear patterns. Reduced product recalls and product safety issues , due to a fully hinged design that allows the belt to backbend over conveyor rollers instead of flexing eliminating component fatigue and breakage. Improved operator safety thanks to safe, interlocking edges that reduce the chances for the moving belt to snag clothing of nearby operators. Fast installation and maintenance that require only a few simple hand tools. Splicing can be done in just a few minutes compared to 15 minutes or longer for some other standard belts. Handling delicate, small products and tight transfers because of a short pitch on the standard 7/16-inch belt. Simplified product stock for users , since the reusable rods can be used for splicing, eliminating the need for extra splice rod stock. Reduced likelihood of belt breakage that can cause product contamination, thanks to an engineered design that ensures picket fracture. The PacTitan Pro is fully customizable, available in varying widths and opening sizes to meet the needs of a wide range of applications in food processing. Get more information about the PacTitan Pro Metal Belt from Regal Rexnord. The Company’s electric motors and air moving subsystems provide the power to create motion. A portfolio of highly engineered power transmission components and subsystems efficiently transmits motion to power industrial applications. The Company’s automation offering, comprised of controllers, drives, precision motors, and actuators, controls motion in applications ranging from factory automation to precision tools used in surgical applications. The Company’s end markets benefit from meaningful secular demand tailwinds, and include factory automation, food & beverage, aerospace, medical, data center, warehouse, alternative energy, residential and commercial buildings, general industrial, construction, metals and mining, and agriculture. Regal Rexnord is comprised of three operating segments: Industrial Powertrain Solutions, Power Efficiency Solutions, and Automation & Motion Control. title: We've partnered with Google to bring Google Wallet credentials to businesses
summary: Authologic has partnered with Google to bring Google Wallet credentials and Google ID Pass to businesses for seamless, digital KYC/AML verification.
body_text: Google Wallet already lets users store verified identity credentials issued by governments, banks, or Google itself on their phones. Using our OmniID platform, businesses can now accept all these credentials, including Google ID Pass, the digital passport available in various countries around the world, including the United States, United Kingdom, Brazil, Singapore, and Taiwan. When a business requests verification, the user can share only the attributes needed, such as a name or age confirmation, directly from their device. OmniID platform connects businesses to a wide range of identity verification methods, including Google Wallet, government eIDs, EUDI wallets, mobile driving licenses, bank-based verification, and biometric checks. The platform automatically selects the most suitable method based on the user’s location and device, while providing fallback options for those who do not yet have a digital credential. Google Wallet is already home to verified identity credentials for users across the world. Our goal has always been to make those credentials accessible to businesses that need them for KYC/AML processes, without requiring a separate integration for every digital wallet or credential type. Our collaboration with Google is a major step toward that. The timing reflects a structural shift in how identity is issued and verified. EU member states must make digital wallets available to citizens by December 2026 under eIDAS 2.0 regulation. Twenty-one US states currently issue mobile driving licenses, and more are likely to follow this year. As governments and institutions issue credentials directly to more people's personal devices, the share of users who can verify their identity digitally will grow, thus reducing overall reliance on the document uploading and manual review processes still driving up KYC costs. Businesses interested in accepting Google Wallet credentials through Authologic can get in touch with us through our website. title: hotglue melt: April 2024
summary: This is your monthly update for April!
body_text: Welcome to our April Melt! Here’s what you may have missed from the past month. New Connectors ⛓️ We added 5 new integrations to our library and the open-source Singer community in April. Logic4 Keyna from our integrations team built a tap and target for Logic4 ( logic4.nl ), an e-commerce and ERP platform based in the Netherlands. You can use the connectors to fetch inventory, purchase, and sales information, and write back transactions like purchase orders. Bird (formerly MessageBird) Keyna built a target for Bird ( bird.com ), an omnichannel communications platform and CRM. Built on Hotglue’s target SDK, the target lets you push any data, like new contacts, to your customers’ Bird CRM accounts. Appsflyer Adil from our integrations team built a target for Appsflyer ( appsflyer.com ), a mobile marketing analytics tool. Combined with our existing Appsflyer tap, the new target allows you to offer bi-directional connectivity with your customers’ Appsflyer apps. Connectwise Our partner, Plentive, built a connector to read data from Connectwise ( connectwise.com ), an MSP management solution. The tap fetches data such as projects, activities, and time entries. ClientTether Chauncy from Plentive also built a connector for ClientTether ( clienttether.com ), a CRM for franchises. The connector fetches general CRM data from your customers’ ClientTether accounts. We also released a Confluence connector out of beta, thanks to a fork of Edgar Ramírez Mondragón ’s Singer tap. New API endpoints 🚥 We released two new API endpoints last month. catalog/search Run fast, granular searches across catalogs to search for streams, fetch types, and more. This is particularly useful for large catalogs that are too big to be served in a single linkedSource fetch. discover/kill Just like the Kill Jobs endpoint, you can use this to end any running discovers for a linked connection. Job log quality of life updates 🔁 You may also notice some minor QoL updates to your log viewing experience: Logs now open with the erroring section loaded, rather than the first line of the log We added new navigation pills to quickly skip between the sync, ETL, and export sections Logs are now clickable as soon as jobs kick off Job-level environment variable control ✅ You have more control than ever over the behavior that your jobs run with. POST /jobs When making a POST to `/jobs`, you can define override environment variables. This could be an existing reserved variable (max_record_count, default_export_format) or a custom environment variable used in your ETL. Schedules When setting schedules, you can now configure schedules to run with specific environment variables and job settings, just like manual job runs. Supported params in schedules now include: override_start_date override_selected_tables override_field_map environment_variables Got questions, or have requests you’d like to see us build? Reach out to us in Slack or at hello@hotglue.xyz . See you next month 🙂 - Brendan TABLE OF CONTENTS RECOMMENDED BLOGS hotglue melt: March 2024 This is your monthly update for March! hotglue melt: February 2024 This is your monthly update for February! hotglue melt: 2023 Feature Roundup This is your 2023 hotglue feature update!
